analysis:
Examined both files' metadata, patches and supplied BASE/HEAD source. The composite action adds SwiftPM repository caching keyed by OS, workspace/home layout, lane and lockfiles (action.yml:43–53), while all three cache saves now require an explicit default-off save-caches input (107, 116, 143). ci.yml supplies that input only for master/dev pushes (19; provider caller at 266), narrowing PR cache writes. The workflow adds daily .git caches, connectivity checks, credential-free checkouts and saves immediately after checkout (57–93 and repeated blocks); full-history documentation caches have a separate key family (163–197). Git fsck checks connectivity, not configuration authenticity, but supplied evidence does not establish an adversarial writer to caches restored by trusted pushes. No supported cache-poisoning or token-disclosure regression was identified.
Also examined sparse checkout exclusions, normalized submodule cache identity (ci.yml:922), cluster save restrictions (960, 965), and conditional audio fixture provisioning (400–414). These changes affect CI availability and build-evidence confidence relevant to A-017/T-054; they do not visibly alter serving authorization, encryption, billing, privileged fan control or T-041 runtime cache isolation.
Integration must reconcile the new needs.changes.outputs.mimo_audio dependency (ci.yml:403, 411) with component-changes.yml and scripts/ci-component-paths.py: confirm output propagation and coverage of native audio/security admission inputs so relevant changes still execute the audio gate. Those implementations are not supplied here, so reduced gate coverage is an unresolved contract, not a finding. Only indexed definitions and selected detailed threat evidence were supplied; this is not a full PR audit.
